transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-10
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Marisol Vega (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Helix Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (Infra), Aisha Khan (Security)

Summary: quick recap of last week, bench numbers vs baseline provider, tuning notes, next steps. Transcript auto-capture; some words may be off.

00:00 Ethan: okay hey everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to review the benchmark numbers we ran this week versus the baseline provider and go over tuning notes. before we start any quick updates?
00:12 Priya: yeah thanks Ethan, quick one from our side - we've started routing a small % of traffic through the on-prem fall back so we have some real-world samples in shared drive, but mostly looking for performance numbers.
00:25 Marisol: great, and I'll walk through the slides - the benchmark runs were 3 x 1 hour steady-state jobs, same prompt set you gave last week, 512 token average, mixed short/long. we compared Redwood dedicated instance with caching/batching enabled vs the baseline provider (their managed endpoint).
00:44 Tom: just to be clear, are we comparing the same model family? baseline was using the 13B variant, correct?
00:51 Marisol: yes, roughly the same model architecture. we used a quantized 13B on Redwood with nvlink-enabled GPUs; baseline was their standard managed 13B. there might be small version diffs so numbers are approximate.
01:06 Priya: ok that's fine, want relative performance.
01:10 Marisol: slide one - p50 latency: Redwood p50 = 72 ms, baseline p50 = 110 ms. p95: Redwood = 420 ms, baseline p95 = 720 ms. throughput sustained (tokens/sec): Redwood steady = 48k tokens/s, baseline = 31k tokens/s. these are for the 1GPU dedicated config with batching window 20ms and kv-cache warm.
01:42 Priya: those p95 numbers look good. can you break out cold start impact?
01:48 Marisol: cold starts we saw a 1.8x increase on both; Redwood cold p95 ~750 ms, baseline cold p95 ~1.2s. but in production you get much fewer colds with persistent sessions + cache.
02:05 Aisha: curious on encryption and where KV cache lives - is it RAM ephemeral only or persisted to disk? any customer data touching disk?
02:13 Marisol: KV cache is in-GPU memory where possible, falls back to node RAM. we don't persist prompt data to disk; for private deployments you can mount encrypted volumes, and we integrate with KMS for disk keys. we'll follow up with the security docs.
02:30 Ethan: noted, Aisha we'll send the SOC2/ISO docs and KMS architecture.
02:36 Aisha: thanks.
02:40 Marisol: next, batching tradeoffs - with a 20ms batching window we saw 30% throughput increase and only a small p50 bump. increasing window to 50ms gave +55% throughput but p50 increased ~40% which gorged latency-sensitive flows.
03:02 Tom: what's the CPU/PCI overhead when you up batch size? we saw some host overhead in our in-house tests on pcie gen3 nodes.
03:10 Marisol: good q. on our infra the host CPU utilization rose ~12% for 50ms windows, and PCIe copy spikes were visible but within healthy margins. we can provide perf counters from the runs.
03:24 Priya: what about KV cache hit rate?
03:28 Marisol: for your prompt set hit rate averaged 68% after warmup, which is why throughput improved a lot. low hit rates cause more compute per request.
03:36 Priya: ok, we can try coalescing more prefixes.
03:40 Ethan: I'd call out one nuance - baseline provider uses automatic model fallback during contention which sometimes increased their p95 due to model switching. Redwood kept the same model but routed to dedicated capacity so p95 remained tighter.
03:58 Priya: did you test error rates at higher loads?
04:02 Marisol: yes, at 1.8x target load baseline started dropping new sessions ~2.5% and occasional 500s; Redwood at 1.8x with autoscaling buffer had <0.3% errors and graceful queuing.
04:18 Tom: any network egress differences we should be aware of?
04:22 Marisol: baseline had slightly lower egress because they compress responses differently; Redwood's bytes per token were marginally higher due to metadata. we'll include bytes per response in the spreadsheet.
04:36 Priya: pricing impact - how does dedicated pricing look vs baseline?
04:42 Ethan: short answer, for your monthly volume the committed dedicated option reduces unit cost ~22% vs our hosted pay-as-you-go. baseline's managed endpoint has slightly lower per-call list price but you see higher tail latency and less consistent throughput which can cost you via retries. we'll send a templated cost model.
05:01 Aisha: on compliance, we need to confirm data residency for logs and how long audit logs retained - for POC we need 90 days retention only.
05:10 Ethan: we'll confirm and map to our retention config; we do 90/365 options and can push to your S3.
05:18 Marisol: tuning notes: quantization to int8 reduced memory footprint and gave similar p50 but increased p95 by ~7% for long sequences; for Helix we recommended int8 + KV cache to get best cost/latency balance.
05:36 Priya: any decoding differences? we saw a slight change in perplexity but not material for our NER extraction tasks.
05:44 Marisol: yes small differences, we'll include eval metrics in the results doc - the qualitative regression was <0.8% on your eval set.
05:52 Tom: can you re-run the 10k run but with our long tail prompts included? last time the baseline had a 30% latency spike on few outliers.
05:59 Marisol: planned — that's the extended run we scheduled next. we'll enable full KV warm start and track outliers.
06:07 Priya: for next steps can you also include a run with reduced batching (10ms) for latency-sensitive route and a separate high-throughput config?
06:13 Marisol: yep we'll produce both configs and a suggested routing policy example.
06:18 Ethan: quick question from my side on go/no-go: what's your timeline for pilot decision?
06:23 Priya: ideally before end of month - engineering signoff and security signoff.
06:28 Ethan: cool, we'll prioritize the extended benchmark and docs to meet that cadence.
06:33 Aisha: one friction - KMS integration: do you require customer-managed keys for private? we prefer CMK in cloud KMS.
06:40 Marisol: we support CMKs; for private installs we can plug into your KMS/HSM and we provide key rotation guidance.
06:47 Aisha: ok please share the architecture diagram.
06:50 Ethan: will do.
06:53 Priya: any surprises in the benchmark logs we should know about?
06:56 Marisol: we had one maintenance-induced node migration during baseline run which slightly skewed one window, we removed that outlier for the final table but note it in notes. also their endpoint throttled some long sequences.
07:12 Tom: sounds like we need to test in our network to check egress latency to your region.
07:16 Ethan: I'll ask infra to coordinate with you Tom on peering tests - put preferred windows in the doc.
07:22 Priya: let's recap next steps.
07:25 Ethan: recap: send pricing + cost model, Marisol to run extended 10k with long-tail and both 10ms/50ms batching configs, Helix to provide 500 sample prompts, Aisha will confirm SOC2/KMS scoping. schedule ops deep dive week of 3/22.
07:42 Priya: sounds good, thanks everyone.
07:45 Aisha: thanks.
07:46 Ethan: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the sheets and the scheduled deep dive invite. bye.

Notes: minor transcription artifacts present (names sometimes mis-typed). Reference artifacts: shared spreadsheet link - /drive/helix-redwood/benchmarks-2026-03-10.xlsx (link in convo), security docs: /docs/redwood-security-scope.pdf.

End of transcript.
